Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 64, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called at-Taghabun (Mutual Loss and Gain), because this word is mentioned in it. It is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, the day on which the disparity between people becomes apparent and the disbelievers' loss becomes clear through their abandonment of faith. The word is not mentioned in any other surah.

The Aims of the Surah

• A warning against denying the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), and a call to take heed from what befell the peoples who denied their messengers and rejected their clear signs, so that punishment and destruction overtook them because of their disbelief, obstinacy and misguidance.

• A rebuke to the polytheists for denying the Resurrection, and a warning to them that they will be confronted with the recompense of their deeds when they are raised. It also clarifies that the salvation of creation lies in faith in Allah alone, in affirming His Messenger (ﷺ) and the Book that he brought, and in belief in the Resurrection.

• A warning to the believers against the enmity of some of their relatives, lest those relatives discourage them from faith, emigration and jihad; an indication to them to be patient with these relatives and with the loss of their wealth which the polytheists had seized; and a command to them to spend in good causes, to fear Allah, and to hear and obey Him; and a warning against stinginess and miserliness.

[The Tafsir]

Everything in the heavens and everything on the earth glorifies Allah, exalting Him above what is not befitting to Him. To Him belongs absolute authority over everything, and to Him belongs all good and beautiful praise, and He is Able over everything.

Allah is the One who brought you into existence from nothingness. So among you are those who deny His divinity, and among you are those who affirm it and act in accordance with His law. He, glorified is He, is All-Seeing of your deeds; nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for them.

God created the heavens and the earth with perfect wisdom, and He created you and gave you the best of forms. To Him is the final return on the Day of Resurrection, when He will recompense each person according to his deeds.

God, glorified and exalted is He, knows everything in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal, O people, among yourselves and what you disclose. And God is All-Knowing of what the breasts harbor and what the souls conceal.

Has there not come to you, O polytheists, the news of those who disbelieved among the nations before you, when the evil consequence of their disbelief and the evil of their deeds befell them in this world? And for them in the Hereafter is a painful, agonizing punishment?

That punishment which befell them in this world, and what awaits them in the Hereafter, is because their messengers from God used to come to them with clear signs and manifest miracles, and they said, denying them: "Shall mere humans guide us?" So they disbelieved in God, rejected the message of His messengers, and turned away from the truth, refusing to accept it. God is free of need of their faith and worship, for God is Ghani (Self-Sufficient, Rich without need), possessing complete and absolute sufficiency, Hamid (Praiseworthy) in His words, deeds, and attributes. He does not care for them, and their misguidance does not harm Him in the least.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 64, verse 7:

The disbelievers who denied Allah claimed falsely that they would never be brought out from their graves after death. Say to them, O Messenger: "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be brought out from your graves alive, then you will surely be informed of what you did in the world. That is easy and simple for Allah."

So believe in Allah and His Messenger, O polytheists, and be guided by the Qur'an that He has sent down to His Messenger. Allah is All-Aware of what you do; nothing of your deeds or your words is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for them on the Day of Resurrection.

Remember the Day of Gathering, when Allah will gather the earlier and the later generations. It is the day on which the loss and the disparity among creatures will become evident, so the believers will gain over the disbelievers and the defiantly disobedient. The people of faith will enter Paradise by the mercy of Allah, and the people of disbelief will enter the Fire by the justice of Allah. Whoever believes in Allah and acts in obedience to Him, Allah will remove his misdeeds from him and admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, from beneath their palaces and trees, abiding therein forever. That abiding in the gardens is the great triumph, after which there is no triumph.

Those who disbelieved, denying that Allah is the true God and rejecting the proofs of His lordship (rubūbiyyah) and the evidences of His divinity (ulūhiyyah) that He sent with His messengers, are the people of the Fire, abiding in it forever. And how wretched is the destination to which they have come, which is Hell (Jahannam).

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 64 (al-Taghabun), verse 11:

No calamity befalls anyone except by the permission of Allah, by His decree and His divine measure. And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart to submit to His command and to be content with His decree, and He guides him to the best of sayings, deeds and states; for the root of guidance lies in the heart, and the limbs follow it. And Allah is All-Knowing of everything; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

And obey Allah, O people, and submit to Him in what He has commanded and what He has forbidden. And obey the Messenger (ﷺ) in what he conveys to you from his Lord. But if you turn away from obeying Allah and His Messenger, then there is no harm upon Our Messenger for your turning away; he is only obligated to convey to you what he was sent with, a clear conveyance.
Allah alone, there is no deity worthy of worship besides Him. And upon Allah let the believers in His oneness rely in all their affairs.

This is the commentary text of al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex) on Surah 64, verse 14, translated as it stands:

O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. And if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

Your wealth and your children are only a trial and a test for you. With Allah is a great reward for whoever gives His obedience precedence over the obedience of others, and who pays the right of Allah from his wealth.

Therefore, O believers, exert your utmost effort and capacity in fearing Allah, listen to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the listening of contemplation and reflection, obey his commands, and avoid his prohibitions. And spend from what Allah has provided you; it will be better for you. And whoever is saved from stinginess and withholding of wealth from bounty, those are the ones who attain every good and succeed in every desire.

If you spend your wealth in the cause of Allah sincerely and with a willing heart, Allah will multiply the reward of what you have spent and forgive your sins. Allah is Most Appreciative (Shakur) toward those who spend, rewarding them well for what they have spent, and Most Forbearing (Halim), not hastening punishment against those who disobey Him.
He is the All-Knowing of everything hidden and everything witnessed, the Almighty who cannot be overpowered, the All-Wise in His sayings and His actions.
